steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
You'll ask Claude to edit the todo.txt you made in Terminal practice 1.

You'll learn two new things today:

  1. How to read the "what will change" screen Claude shows before editing
  2. How to say no and ask again when you don't like it
  • Time: 10–15 minutes
  • You need: the computer you used for Terminal practice 1 (todo.txt in the Practice folder on your desktop)

faq.a: In Terminal practice 1 you install Claude Code and create todo.txt. Please start with Terminal practice 1.

steps.title: Which computer are you using?
steps.html: Pick the computer you used for Terminal practice 1.

steps.title: Start Claude Code again

win.html:
Same as 'Open the window in the practice folder' in Terminal practice 1.

  1. Double-click the Practice folder on your desktop.
  2. Click the address bar at the top of the folder window, type powershell and press Enter.
  3. Type claude in the window and press Enter.

You only sign in the first time. This time the typing box appears right away.

mac.html:
Same as 'Open the window in the practice folder' in Terminal practice 1.

  1. Open Terminal. (⌘ command+space → Terminal → return)
  2. Type cd and a space, drag the Practice folder from your desktop onto the window, and press return.
  3. Type claude and press return.

You only sign in the first time. This time the typing box appears right away.

steps.alt: The typing box appears as soon as Claude Code starts

check.q: Do you see the box to type in (with a > sign)?

steps.title: If starting it again doesn't work
steps.html:
• If you see 'claude' is not recognized, close the window and open it again. If it still doesn't work, restart the computer.
  • If it asks you to sign in again, do it like the sign-in step in Terminal practice 1.
  • Not sure? See that step in Terminal practice 1 again.

steps.title: First, ask it to read the file
steps.html: Paste or type the sentence below into the box and press Enter (return on a Mac).

check.q: Did the contents of todo.txt appear on screen?

steps.title: If it can't find the file
steps.html:
• Claude only sees files in the folder where you opened the window. Check that you opened it in the practice folder.
  • If your file has a different name (e.g. 할일.txt), say that name instead.
  • If there's no todo.txt, create it first: "Create a file called todo.txt and write 3 example to-dos for today".

steps.title: Notice it didn't ask permission?
steps.html:
When it only reads a file, nothing changes. So Claude shows it without asking.

It only asks permission when it creates or edits a file. Now let's ask it to make an edit.

steps.title: Ask it to make an edit
steps.html: Ask it to change the second line.
steps.code: In todo.txt, change line 2 to "Set up a lunch meeting"
steps.alt: The screen showing changes with red and green lines

check.q: Did a screen with red and green lines appear, like the picture?

steps.title: If you see a different screen
steps.html:
• Claude may still be thinking. Wait a few seconds.
  • If Claude asks something back (e.g. which line), type your answer and press Enter.
  • If it already says it made the change, you may have chosen option 2 (don't ask again) before. It's fine to move on to checking the result.

steps.title: How to read the "what will change" screen
steps.html:
It looks strange at first, but just look at the colors.

- Red lineText that will be removed
+ Green lineText that will be added
Uncolored lineText that stays the same

Do you want to make this edit…? at the bottom means "May I make this change?"

  • 1. Yes — yes, make the change
  • 2. Yes, allow all edits… — don't ask again, just make every change → don't choose this for now
  • 3. No… — no, do it differently

If the red line shows the old line 2 and the green line shows Set up a lunch meeting, it's what you asked for. Press Enter on 1. Yes.

check.noLabel: The red and green lines look wrong

steps.title: If the changes aren't what you asked for
steps.html:
That's exactly when to choose 3. No. Press ↓ twice to reach option 3 and press Enter (or press Esc), then say it again, e.g. "Change only line 2 to 'Set up a lunch meeting'".

The to-dos in your file are examples Claude chose in Terminal practice 1, so it's fine if the words differ from the picture. Just check that line 2 changes.

steps.title: See the result with your own eyes

win.html:
1. In the practice folder, double-click todo.txt. Notepad opens.
  2. Check that line 2 now says Set up a lunch meeting.
  3. Once you've checked, close Notepad with the ✕ at the top right. Leaving it open while Claude edits again can be confusing.

mac.html:
1. In the practice folder, double-click todo.txt. TextEdit opens.
  2. Check that line 2 now says Set up a lunch meeting.
  3. Once you've checked, close TextEdit with the red circle at the top left.

steps.alt: Checking in Notepad that line 2 changed

check.q: Does line 2 now say 'Set up a lunch meeting'?

steps.title: If you don't see the change
steps.html:
• If you opened Notepad before the edit, close it and open it again.
  • Ask Claude, "Show me what todo.txt says now."
  • If you pressed 3. No, the file didn't change. Go back to the edit step and try again.

steps.title: Press "No" on purpose
steps.html: Now let's practice what to do when you don't like something. Pressing No doesn't change the file at all, so don't worry.
steps.code: Add a title at the top of the to-do list

check.q: When you see the title Claude chose, press ↓ twice to reach 3. No and press Enter (or Esc). Did the typing box come back?

steps.title: If choosing No doesn't work
steps.html:
• Press the down arrow (↓) key twice to move the marker to 3. No…, then press Enter.
  • An easier way: press Esc (top left of the keyboard) once.
  • If you pressed Yes by mistake, just say "Undo the change you just made."

steps.title: Say what you want instead
steps.html: After pressing No, just say what you want.

check.q: Did you see '+ Today's to-dos' as a green line and press 1. Yes?

steps.title: 🎉 Terminal practice 2 done! What you learned
steps.html:
You checked changes before they happened, and asked again when needed.

Three things to remember

  1. It doesn't ask when it reads a file; it only asks when it creates or edits one.
  2. On the before-edit screen, red lines will be removed and green lines will be added.
  3. If you don't like it, choose No (or Esc) and say it again. The file stays as it was.

Why does this matter?

AI sometimes changes things differently from what you asked. As long as you have the habit of reading the changes before pressing Yes, your files won't change unexpectedly. It's the most important habit for using AI agents safely.

Next step

In the next practice you'll learn how to start a new conversation and pick up where you left off the next day.
